checkpoints.description: [1/2] Centralize BOM tolerance: export withoutBom from fs-atomic and use it in the shipped-preset reader, the tuner lane reader and the existing receipt/profile readers; failing-first tests for a BOM preset and a BOM profile lane; [2/2] npm test, aikit check, ADR-139, UI review, commit (not a generation-path change)

impact_assessment.why: A preset or profile saved with a UTF-8 BOM by a Windows editor is silently dropped (preset never applies) or silently runs the tune on the CPU lane, because only some JSON readers strip the BOM
impact_assessment.benefits: One tolerance rule for every hand-editable state file; a shared helper replaces three inline copies
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none (same parsed value); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: reads only
impact_assessment.mitigation: tests pin the BOM case for presets and lanes; the helper strips only a leading U+FEFF; all existing readers keep their fallbacks

checkpoints.description: [1/2] IDEA-0995 backend: a pure resolver (hf:org/repo@rev/folder/file.gguf or huggingface.co resolve/blob links only, https only, plain segments, .gguf only, canonical resolve URL), DownloadManager.inspectSource (HEAD through the existing redirect token gate, requires a positive Content-Length, caps user files at 32 GiB, maps 404/401/403), DownloadManager.startSource (job carries its URL and quant, no catalog id; receipt records the URL; resume identity and dedupe keep one job per file), and POST /api/models/add-hf (loopback only, resolve before any fetch, optional pinned SHA-256). 12 failing-first tests; [2/2] npm test, live HEAD check, aikit check, ADR-140, UI follows in a separate task (G-001 not applicable: no generation path)

impact_assessment.why: The curated catalog is the only download path; IDEA-0995 is the biggest user unlock, but arbitrary URLs need guardrails before any code accepts them
impact_assessment.benefits: A user can add one exact HF GGUF with a validated URL, real size and optional pin; the download, resume, header check and receipt paths are reused unchanged
impact_assessment.risks: contract: DownloadManager gains inspectSource/startSource and jobs may carry a null catalog id; dependency: none; concurrency: remote jobs share the two-slot limit and dedupe by file; state: receipts record the URL and a null catalog id
impact_assessment.mitigation: resolver is pure and rejects before any network; token stays behind the existing redirect gate; size is mandatory and capped; a pinned hash still verifies; catalog path is covered by existing tests and unchanged when job.url is absent

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Refuse a user-chosen source whose file name already exists unless its install receipt names the same URL and size, in which case the add is idempotent and returns a complete job without fetching; never overwrite or claim success for a different file. Failing-first tests for conflict, idempotent add and another-URL receipt; [2/2] npm test, aikit check, ADR-142, UI review, commit (G-001 not applicable: download path only)

impact_assessment.why: startSource reused the catalog early-complete check, so an existing same-named, same-sized file made the add report success with no receipt, and a same-named file of another size would be atomically replaced: a pasted link could overwrite a catalog model
impact_assessment.benefits: A colliding name is refused with a clear Fix instead of overwriting or faking a completed download; re-adding the same URL is a no-op
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one new 409 code on the source path; dependency: none; concurrency: the existing per-file starting set still serializes starts; state: none written on a refusal
impact_assessment.mitigation: the receipt URL+size is the identity; catalog starts keep their current behaviour; tests pin the file bytes are unchanged after a refusal

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Refuse a split GGUF part (name matching -00001-of-00002.gguf) in the Hugging Face resolver with a Fix that points at the single-file quantization; leave names that merely contain of or digits alone. Failing-first resolver tests; [2/2] npm test, aikit check, ADR-143, UI review, commit (G-001 not applicable: resolver only)

impact_assessment.why: A split part downloads like any GGUF, then the library's spliceSplitFiles:false scan and the loader cannot use it alone, so the user pays a multi-GB download for a model that cannot load
impact_assessment.benefits: The refusal happens before any network request and names the reason; single-file quants keep working
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one more invalid reference (a file that could never load); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: the pattern requires the five-digit HF split suffix, so ordinary names with of or digits are unaffected; tests cover both sides

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Keep the Hugging Face host rule in one exported helper (assertHuggingFaceFileUrl) and call it from inspectSource and startSource too, so a direct caller can never send the token to a non-Hugging-Face first hop or download another host; refuse a non-string SHA-256 instead of ignoring it. Failing-first tests for both methods; [2/2] npm test, a full pinned live import in a temp home (download, header check, promotion, receipt, Installed line), aikit check, ADR-144, UI review, commit (G-001 not applicable: download path only)

impact_assessment.why: Only the route enforced the host; the methods are exported and one direct call would send the HF token on the first request to any host and could download any https file, and a numeric sha256 was silently dropped
impact_assessment.benefits: The guardrail lives in one module and every source entry point enforces it; a mistyped pin is refused instead of unpinning the file
impact_assessment.risks: contract: source methods refuse non-HF URLs and non-string pins; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: the canonical resolver URL and www host still pass; catalog downloads do not use these methods; tests pin both refusals and no engine/job is created
